subject.title: feat(ui): session unarchive flows with undo toast

question: Should the Control UI ship the proposed archived-session recovery UX, including a bounded “Delete all archived” action, as the supported archive-management flow?
rationale: The implementation adds a new user-facing recovery and destructive-management workflow rather than repairing a defined broken API contract; the protected maintainer label requires human product ownership of that behavior.

options.title: Approve the recovery workflow
options.body: Accept undo, restore, archived navigation, and the exact-count guarded bulk-delete behavior after refreshing review and checks on the current head.

options.title: Keep recovery, narrow deletion
options.body: Land the undo and restore UI but remove or redesign bulk deletion until maintainers choose an unbounded or explicitly limited archive-management contract.

options.title: Pause for UX direction
options.body: Hold the PR until the intended archive-management behavior and destructive-action limits are decided by the Control UI owners.

recommendation.title: Approve the recovery workflow
recommendation.body: Accept undo, restore, archived navigation, and the exact-count guarded bulk-delete behavior after refreshing review and checks on the current head.

likelyOwner.reason: They can explain the current UX and bounded-delete tradeoff, while a Control UI owner should make the final product decision.
